scope.role: Advisory only. A classifier output must never by itself produce a definitive high-risk / fraud decision. Person 2's decision engine is not modified.

anonymisation.definition: anon-v1 unchanged, then @handles (letter/underscore start, <= 30 chars) -> handletoken; residual e-mail fragments with a letter on both sides of '@' and dangling local parts -> emailtoken. Rates/prices and standalone '@' kept.
anonymisation.regression_tests: tests/test_anonymiser_versions.py (anon-v1 golden outputs frozen; anon-v2 behaviour)
anonymisation.applied_to: Every row of every source, both classes, train and test. Models trained under v4 record preprocessing='anon-v2' and classify_text() applies it before vectorising.

build_order: 1. Verify this protocol's SHA-256; verify pinned source hashes; never modify raw files.
2. Map labels; exclude ambiguous IMC25 labels, non-English IMC25 rows and non-Latin Mendeley rows; log every exclusion with reason (no text).
3. Investigate >= 10-digit runs (IMC25, Mendeley); anonymise all rows with anon-v2; STOP if any >= 4-digit run remains.
4. Remove rows overlapping the retired benchmark or the challenge suite (exact normalised, skeleton, Jaccard >= 0.8, both sides anonymised with anon-v2).
5. Exact normalised de-duplication, priority DONATION > IMC25 > MWOZ_TEST > MWOZ_TRAIN > MENDELEY > R115 > SYN; identical text with conflicting labels -> all copies excluded.
7. Grouping G4 steps 2-3: giant-unit rule and deterministic test assignment.
8. Grouping G4 step 4: purge TRAIN rows within the purge threshold of any TEST row; STOP if any cross-split pair remains.
10. Write pool and test; seal. Reports are counts only.

grouping.step_1_atomic_units: Within each source, link rows whose skeleton_text(anon-v2) token sets have Jaccard >= 0.8 (exact similarity join, text_classifier.jaccard_pairs), plus base-key links. Atomic unit = connected component. Units are never split: splitting one would place a Jaccard >= 0.8 pair (the leakage definition) across the split.
grouping.unit_id: <source>:<smallest stable row key in the unit>
grouping.step_2_giant_units: For test-eligible sources (IMC25, DONATION): a unit with more rows than max(50, floor(0.01 x rows of that source after step 5)) is assigned to TRAIN, never TEST. Deterministic, size-based, independent of labels and model output.
grouping.step_3_assignment: Other IMC25 and DONATION units: TEST if int(sha256(salt + '|' + unit_id).hexdigest()[:8], 16) / 2**32 < 0.20, else TRAIN. MWOZ_TEST rows all TEST; MWOZ_TRAIN, MENDELEY, R115, SYN all TRAIN.
grouping.step_4_purge: Every TRAIN row (any source) that has exact-normalised equality, skeleton equality, or skeleton-token Jaccard >= 0.6 with ANY TEST row is removed from the pool (row level). TEST is never altered. Final verification: zero cross-split pairs at Jaccard >= 0.6, zero exact and skeleton matches.
grouping.rationale: Counts-only diagnostics (reports/grouping_v4/diagnostics.json) showed single-link at 0.6 chains distinct campaigns into one 1,685-row unit (22 institutions; sampled internal median Jaccard 0.33; 9.6 % of pairs < 0.2) that could be ~41 % of the test if drawn. Single-link at 0.8 is the smallest leakage-safe unit (largest 806). Forcing giant units to TRAIN bounds test domination (largest test unit 0.9-3.6 % of test across six diagnostic salts) without splitting units; the 0.6 purge removes near-template variants of test rows from training, stricter than v3's 0.8 leakage check.
trade_offs: The largest template families (diagnostics: 3 IMC25 units, 1,122 rows, SBI/HDFC KYC-style) are never in the test, so S1/S2 do not measure them.
Hash assignment stays at 20 % of eligible units; the realised TEST share of IMC25 rows is lower (diagnostics: 17-19 %).
Purging removes roughly 2,000-2,200 IMC25 TRAIN rows (diagnostics).
Atomic 0.8 units can still be internally heterogeneous (806-row unit: sampled median Jaccard 0.42), but cannot be split without violating the leakage definition.
grouping.reporting: Report unit-size distribution per source, forced-TRAIN units/rows, test share of rows, largest test unit and its share of the test, purged rows per source, and the final cross-split check.

minimum_legitimate_coverage.test_requirement: Frozen test must contain >= 150 donated messages from >= 5 donors, with >= 3 categories having >= 25 messages each.
minimum_legitimate_coverage.if_not_met: Criterion L1 is NOT EVALUABLE; the model can at most be reported as 'scam recall evaluated; false positives on genuine Indian financial alerts NOT validated'. MENDELEY rows never count toward this requirement.

model_selection.data: Pool v5 TRAIN rows only; the frozen test is never read (sealed-file guard).
model_selection.cv: StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) over pool units

candidates.A_v1_config: word 1-2-grams, letters-only tokens, sublinear TF, C=1.0, class_weight=balanced
candidates.G_char_wb_3_5: char_wb 3-5-grams, min_df=2, sublinear TF, C=1.0, class_weight=balanced

model_selection.rule: Maximise pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 among candidates whose out-of-fold FPR on DONATION rows is <= 0.10 (applied only if the pool has >= 50 DONATION rows). Ties within 0.005 -> lower out-of-fold legitimate FPR -> alphabetical.
reported_baselines: majority class of each training fold (per fold; no held-out label chooses the class)
model_selection.final_training: Selected configuration trained with text_classifier.train(preprocessing='anon-v2') on pool v5 into satyalens_analysis/models/candidates/v5/. The deployed artifact is not replaced by this protocol.
model_selection.scoring: Inconclusive predictions (no in-vocabulary feature) are scored as 'legitimate' in every selection quantity - pooled and per-fold macro-F1, legitimate FPR, DONATION FPR and per-source metrics: a MISS for suspicious rows, NOT a false positive for legitimate rows. Inconclusive counts are reported. Same convention as acceptance_criteria.conventions.
model_selection.baselines_role: Baselines are reported only and are never selection criteria.

acceptance_criteria.conventions: Inconclusive suspicious rows count as MISSES; inconclusive legitimate rows count as NOT false positives; this applies to every acceptance quantity (S1, S2, L1, L2, M1, B1 and all reported breakdowns). Each criterion reports numerator and denominator (macro-F1: row count and confusion matrix). Thresholds are compared on exact values (k/n fractions, unrounded macro-F1); reported values are rounded to 4 dp. acceptance_v5.json (scripts/acceptance_v5.py) is the authoritative criteria result; evaluation.json (text_classifier.evaluate) excludes inconclusive rows from its metrics and is descriptive only.
acceptance_criteria.S1: Suspicious recall on IMC25 test rows >= 0.80
acceptance_criteria.S2: Suspicious recall on India-linked IMC25 test rows >= 0.80
acceptance_criteria.L1: False-positive rate on DONATION test rows <= 0.10 (requires minimum coverage, else NOT EVALUABLE)
acceptance_criteria.B1: Macro-F1 on the full test strictly greater (unrounded) than both the rule-engine baseline and the majority-class baseline on the same test. The majority class is fixed BEFORE evaluation from the training-pool label counts recorded in the sealed manifest (pool_counts), never from test labels.
reported_not_gating: S1 restricted to IMC25 'hey mum/dad' test rows (numerator/denominator), with an explicit small-sample warning
RETROSPECTIVE REFERENCE: macro-F1 of a test-majority predictor, labelled as such; never gating, never used for selection or tuning
acceptance_criteria.verdict: VALIDATED only if S1, S2, L1, L2, M1 and B1 all pass. If L1 is NOT EVALUABLE: at most 'PARTIALLY EVALUATED — not validated for genuine financial alerts'. Any failure: 'NOT VALIDATED'. Even if VALIDATED, the classifier remains advisory-only.

sealing.manifest: reports/frozen_test_v5_manifest.json with sealed_files [{path, sha256}], protocol_file 'docs/protocol_v5.json', protocol_sha256, evaluation_log 'reports/frozen_test_v5_evaluations.jsonl', counts, pool_counts (training label counts by source) and pool_csv_sha256.
sealing.guard: text_classifier loaders refuse files listed in the v5, v4 or v3 manifest (whichever exist) or any byte-identical copy, unless evaluate(final_sealed=True). SATYALENS_SEALED_MANIFEST adds one further manifest to these defaults; it never disables them.
sealing.one_shot: evaluate --final-sealed-evaluation refuses if the protocol hash differs, the sealed file changed, or the evaluation log already has an entry.
sealing.script_rule: Selection and training scripts load data only through the package loaders and never reference frozen_test_v5.csv; enforced by tests.
sealing.commit_record: The sealed manifest is committed to git at sealing. Immediately after the single final evaluation, the evaluation log and the metrics-only reports (evaluation.json, summary.md, acceptance_v5.json, acceptance_v5.md) are committed; the commit history is the authoritative record of the one evaluation. predictions.csv (per-row test labels) is never committed.
sealing.residual_risk: Someone with local write access could delete the evaluation log and re-run the evaluation before the post-evaluation commit; no local control prevents this. Any evidence of a second evaluation of the same sealed test SHA-256 invalidates the result.

.gitignore covers the v4 and v5 pool and frozen test files and evaluation predictions.csv.
before_selection_and_evaluation: scripts/select_text_model_v5.py and scripts/acceptance_v5.py (new; pinned to this protocol's SHA-256; v4 scripts unchanged).

withdrawal.before_sealing: Remove the donor's rows and rebuild.
withdrawal.after_sealing_before_evaluation: Delete the rows, rebuild pool and test under this protocol (same salt), write a new manifest; record the reseal.
withdrawal.after_evaluation: Delete the rows and any copies; keep published aggregates; annotate the report.

deviations: Any deviation after hashing must be recorded with reason and requires a new protocol version (and a new test set if made after the v4 test exists).
